Definition: from G846 and the same as G140; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary:--of own accord, willing of self.
BiblicalUsage: The Macedonians gave beyond their power, willing of themselves, and Titus accepted Paul's exhortation and went to Corinth of his own accord. The word means voluntary, chosen by oneself and not forced.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the freest giving is the giving no one demands, because it shows a heart already won.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
